newsitem.title: FRANCE: French customs seize new gene-altered maize cargo.
newsitem.headline: French customs seize new gene-altered maize cargo.

text.p: French customs officers this week seized a second cargo of U.S. by-products believed to contain genetically-modified maize in the western port of Saint- Nazaire.
A cargo of 3,000 to 4,000 tonnes of maize by-products coming from the United States was held in the Montoir terminal for testing, customs officials said on Thursday.
The freighter Lake Charles unloaded the cargo on January 5 for Britanny-based grain importer Soules.
The case has been referred to the public prosecutor of Nantes and the cargo may be held for 15 days or more, they said.
In December the European Commission cleared imports of genetically-modified maize developed by Swiss firm Ciba-Geigy for sale in Europe.
But environmental organisation Greenpeace and consumer groups oppose imports of genetically-modified crops on the grounds that they may be a risk to human health.
In December protestors from Greenpeace invaded Saint-Nazaire port to prevent the unloading of what they said was the first shipment of U.S. maize to Europe.
The cargo from the Greek freighter Madga P is still being held in the Montoir terminal.
When the EU cleared the sale of gene-altered maize it said it would revise laws to allow for the labelling of goods containing genetically modified material.
France has said it would approve the sale and production of genetically-modified maize only when EU labelling rules are in place.
But if the EU does not move fast enough, France plans to come up with its own labelling rules. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
